title: Twelve of 480 selected Allen mouse response pairs need summed waveform error above 1 percent under causal filtering
abstract: We tested how much paired fitted current and voltage response shapes must change before a causal nonnegative filter can link them. Cumulative response area and Fourier modulus give direct lower bounds on summed total-variation error without inverse filtering. After decay-limit screening in Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1, the bound exceeds 1 percent for 12 of 480 main mouse V1 pairs, 6 of 262 early mouse pairs and 7 of 160 human pairs. It exceeds 5 percent for 10, 4 and 6 pairs. The bound does not exceed 1 percent for most exact inverse-filter sign failures; their minimum correction remains unresolved. Shapes are onset-aligned and normalized. These are finite-sample checks on fitted shapes, not measured uncertainty or evidence against passive neurons. Separate clamp states, somatic current distortion, fit-family limits and selected slices limit interpretation. Original code, proof, aggregate results, a figure, hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Lower bounds on summed total-variation waveform correction in the decay-screened samples. A small bound does not establish that a small correction is sufficient.

citations.reason: Prior exact inverse-filter test. We use its selection definition and compare sign counts with direct waveform error bounds; no code or tables reused.
Prior shared-filter moment-error bounds. This report tests separate per-connection filters and waveform total variation.
